first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that simplifying onboarding can improve both without a documented retention tradeoff. Promotional pricing directly addresses competitor pricing but has known 30-day retention harm, conflicting with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective. Verification should confirm the onboarding effects, segment scope, and durability before launch.

final.rationale: Run a standard guarded experiment simplifying the onboarding flow, focused on self-serve SMB accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, though retention declined 1%. Measure qualified revenue and retention alongside completion and activation, and do not extrapolate beyond SMB without evidence. Avoid promotional pricing because its known retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term revenue.
